exposure: fetal-open surgical technique (OSBAR) for myelomeningocele (MMC) closure
fetal-endoscopic surgical technique (FSBAR) for myelomeningocele (MMC) closure
neonatal surgical technique (NSBAR) for myelomeningocele (MMC) closure
outcome: neuromuscular integrity (segmental alterations in muscle ultrasound density)
likelihood of intervention-related gain in ambulation
cohort: The cohort consisted of children with spina bifida aperta (SBA) who received fetal-open (OSBAR, n=17), fetal-endoscopic (FSBAR, n=13), or neonatal (NSBAR) surgical closure for myelomeningocele (MMC).
finding: Compared to neonatal intervention, fetal interventions (OSBAR and FSBAR) were associated with improved neuromuscular integrity, better segmental neurological outcomes, reduced shunt dependency, and a higher chance of ambulation, with no significant differences found between OSBAR and FSBAR techniques.
